does: Cuts food into even, square-sided sticks.
how: Peel the vegetable and trim its sides flat to make a block.
Slice the block into slabs as thick as the sticks you want.
Stack a few slabs and cut them lengthwise into sticks as wide as the slabs are thick.
Keep the trimmings for a soup or a mash.

cues.text: Sticks with flat faces and square corners, all of one thickness, so that they cook in the same time.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting from a round vegetable without squaring it first, so that the sticks come out as wedges.
mistakes.fix: Trim the sides flat before you slice.

mistakes.mistake: Slabs of uneven thickness, so that thin sticks burn while thick ones stay raw.
mistakes.fix: Hold the knife straight and take the same width at every cut.

comes_after.why: Batons start as thick, even slices.
